==Copyright==
We have had a complaint about users here taking text without permission from encyclopaedia-wot.org. This is not permitted and all content must be original or used with attribution from a site with content that is available under the GFDL. encyclopaedia-wot.org is not under a free license so text from there should never be used here. I have deleted some pages, mostly created by unregistered users, which were clearly copied from there and another wot site. If you are aware of any other pages that were copied, please ask an [[Special:Listadmins|admin]] or [[Special:Listusers/staff|staff]] to delete them. Thanks. [[w:User:Angela|Angela]] <sup>[[User talk:Angela|talk]]</sup> 18:13, 14 March 2007 (UTC)
*Couldn't you have just edited the articles? I mean, did you really have to delete them? Sorry if I offend, [[User:Darth Metus|Insane Ta&#39;veren Number 4]] 19:44, 14 March 2007 (UTC)

:Unfortunately, the very first edit of the ones I deleted was the copyright violation, meaning any subsequent edits were derivative versions which are also violations of copyright. This means they need to be recreated without using the content of that first edit. [[w:User:Angela|Angela]] <sup>[[User talk:Angela|talk]]</sup> 19:54, 14 March 2007 (UTC)

::I have not yet had time to go through the deletion log, but I have undid a number of reversions for which I could not find an indication of copyright violation.  On some others I undid the reversion and added links to the GFDL site they were derived from. --[[User:Gherald|Gherald]] 07:12, 15 March 2007 (UTC)

Well, this is a lovely situation to return to :(  I hadn't read this when I wrote the response on [[User talk:Aristoc#Copyright|my Talk page]]; this at least explains what prompted the deletions. Speaking for myself, as an editor having had articles removed, I have to say I have never even visited encyclopaedia-wot, and not for lack of trying: I've never been able to connect to the site, it always times-out, in fact I didn't think it was even online anymore. I therefore find it hard to credit that my chapter summaries bear much relation to theirs other than they describe the same source material. Regarding Angela's clarification above, if it was the article skeleton structure in violation, and not the content itself, why delete only a handful of articles? Apologies for bleating about 'my' articles, but I know where I stand regarding them, at least. [[User:Aristoc|Aristoc]] 18:10, 15 March 2007 (UTC)
:No, the skeletons are not copyrightable; they're just formatting and metadata.  The violations in question are pretty much the body of summary pages.  I've gone through the deletion log now and restored skeletons from the pages with copyright violations I could identify.  Furthermore, I restored all pages for which I could not immediately locate a violation... please help double-check. --[[User:Gherald|Gherald]] 06:22, 16 March 2007 (UTC)
::I just figured out a way accessing the encyclopaedia-wot pages using Google's cached pages, so I'll try and go through them when I get a moment. I see that their chapter summaries generally run to one or two paragraphs, which makes it even harder to understand why the two that I wrote could be taken for plagiarism! Thanks, Gherald, for restoring them. [[User:Aristoc|Aristoc]] 12:44, 16 March 2007 (UTC)

===Guidelines===
Everyone's assistance in dealing with copyright violations is appreciated, but to facilitate cooperation please observe the following guidelines: --[[User:Gherald|Gherald]] 07:12, 15 March 2007 (UTC)
#Do not revert edits that include GFDL content from other sites for being "copyright violations".  They are more specifically license violations which should be corrected by adding the appropriate link and -- if you want to be even more helpful -- warning the submitting user who neglected to do so.
#When reverting non-website copyright violations, please use the edit summary to name the work in question for reference.
#For reversions of website copyright violations (the most common type), please link back to the website in your edit summary, e.g. "rv copyright violation of http://example.com".
#For encyclopaedia-wot.org in particular, please also use [[Template:ewot]] to add a link to their article under ==External links==
